note: ALL DATA FABRICATED. No firm documents were used. Interim stand-in corpus only.

files.structure: المادة (1)-(9) Arabic articles; Article 1-8 English; tables; signature/stamp box
quirks: Arabic drawn via arabic-reshaper + python-bidi, so the PDF stores PRESENTATION FORMS IN VISUAL ORDER -- realistic reproduction of Arabic DTP output and the main fixture for rtl_fix repair
5-column bilingual payment table with mixed Arabic/Latin headers
Arabic-Indic digits (٢٬٤٥٠٬٠٠٠) alongside Western digits in the table
mixed-direction clause bodies (English defined terms inside Arabic)
signature/stamp box as a bordered table

files.structure: Word Heading 1/2 styles carrying المادة (n) labels; 5-col Table Grid; explicit page break
quirks: DOCX has no stored pagination -- page numbers come from the single explicit page break only; pipeline warns about this
logical-order Arabic (unlike the PDF fixture) -- rtl_fix should NOT repair this one, which is the negative test
Arabic-Indic digits inside table cells

files.language_mix: English primary with Arabic clauses interleaved (true bilingual mix)
quirks: clause numbering is decimal (1.1, 2.3) not المادة -- exercises the English CLAUSE marker pattern and auto-granularity at CLAUSE level
Arabic and English clauses alternate inside the same section, so chunk-level language should come out 'ar-en' for several chunks
bilingual headings contain both scripts on one line -- an rtl_fix mixed_direction flag is expected here

files.structure: الباب / الفصل / المادة hierarchy including 'المادة (7) مكرر'; أولاً-ثالثاً enumerators; (أ)(ب)(ج) sub-clauses
quirks: full statute hierarchy: BOOK > CHAPTER > ARTICLE -- auto granularity should settle on ARTICLE, not sub-clause
'مكرر' (bis) article numbering, an Egyptian legislative convention that naive numeric parsers drop
no pagination at all (TXT) -- every chunk should report page=1
cross-references ('المادة (4)', 'المادة (7)') inside body text that must NOT be treated as boundaries

files.language_mix: heavily mixed Arabic/English in the same sentences
quirks: code-switching mid-sentence ('البند (5) delay penalty cap محدد بنسبة ١٠٪')
Arabic-Indic dates ١٥/٠٣/٢٠٢٦ mixed with Western dates 20/03/2026
this is the primary fixture for rtl_fix mixed_direction and numeral_direction_ambiguous flags -- flags here are EXPECTED, not a bug
DELIBERATELY DAMAGED: stored in VISUAL order with presentation forms, reproducing what broken PDF extraction and some OCR output look like
ground truth for this file is synthetic_statute_ar.txt -- rtl_fix should detect presentation forms and flag/repair reading order
structural markers will NOT match until presentation forms are folded, so this also tests that normalize runs before structure annotation

files.language_mix: Arabic primary, one English heading line
files.structure: البند (1)-(3) clause markers; signature block; two stamps
quirks: image input -- must route straight to OCR with no text layer
round company stamp and rectangular incoming-mail stamp OVERLAP the signature area; OCR is expected to emit junk boxes from the stamps
handwritten-style signature squiggles (non-text ink)
page degraded: 0.7 deg skew, gaussian noise, slight blur, JPEG q72
Arabic-Indic digits in dates and percentages

files.language_mix: bilingual Arabic/English column headers and cells
files.structure: 5-column BORDERLESS table (only a header rule and a total rule)
quirks: borderless table -- PyMuPDF find_tables has no ruling lines to work with; this is the case Docling's TableFormer is meant to cover, and on the OCR path neither applies, so table structure is expected to degrade to reading-order text. KNOWN GAP, see evaluation report.
column contents alternate direction (Arabic label, Latin milestone, Western numerals) -- worst case for line-level reading order
degraded: -0.4 deg skew, noise, JPEG q80
exercises: rtl_fix reading order on table rows

files.structure: as in the source statute/constitution (المادة / Article numbering)
quirks: rasterized at 200 dpi, skew 0.6 deg, gaussian noise sigma 6, blur 0.4, JPEG quality 78
NO text layer -- type_detection must classify this as 'scanned' and route every page to OCR
character-level ground truth available, so OCR accuracy is measurable per language
OPTIMISTIC vs real firm scans: clean glyph rendering, no scanner optics, no photocopy generations, no staple shadows or bleed-through

GROUND TRUTH CAVEAT: the source PDF extracts with spurious intra-word spacing ('دس تور' for 'دستور'), so the reference disagrees with correctly-spaced OCR output on most word boundaries. Space-sensitive CER/WER against this file overstate the error; the space-insensitive CER is the meaningful figure.
